    Weaving in one minute
    

    
  
  
    A loom holds long vertical warp threads, one per column. Each warp thread passes through a heddle on one of eight shafts. To weave a row (a pick) you lift some shafts, which raises every thread on them, and pass the weft thread across. A raised thread shows its own color in that row; everywhere else the weft covers it. Row after row, patterns appear from nothing but the threading and the order of lifts.
    

    


    A LOOM program describes that process. Its output is a grid of color letters, one per crossing, with . for rows never woven. The Cloth tab paints that grid with the palette's colors; Loom & debugger replays it pick by pick.
    


    Statements
    

    
  
    loom W HMust come first. W warp threads (1–200) and room for H picks (1–200).
    
  
    palette k=#rrggbb …Names colors with single letters a–z.
    
  
    warp seqColors every warp thread. The sequence repeats across the width.
    
  
    thread seqPuts each thread on a shaft 1–8, repeating like warp.
    
  
    treadle N liftSaves a lift as treadle N (1–10), used later as tN.
    
  
    shuttle seqWeft colors taken in turn by picks that don't name a color.
    
  
    pick [color] liftWeaves one row with that weft color and lift.
    
  
    cross I JSwaps the threads in columns I and J (color and shaft).
    
  
    drift N / drift -NRotates every thread N columns to the right (or left), wrapping around.
    
  
    maxfloat NFrom here on, stops with an error if a float is longer than N.
    
  
    repeat N { … }Runs the lines in between N times (1–1000). Blocks nest.
    

    

    One statement per line. // starts a comment.
    


    Sequences
    

    
  
    a b cthree elements
    
  
    a*3a a a
    
  
    (a b)*2a b a b
    
  
    mirror(a b c)a b c b a (there and back without repeating the turn)
    
  
    1-4, 4-11 2 3 4 and 4 3 2 1 (shaft sequences only)
    

    


    Lifts
    

    
  
    13shafts 1 and 3
    
  
    - / *no shafts / all shafts
    
  
    !12every shaft except 1 and 2
    
  
    t2whatever treadle 2 lifts (in pick only)
    

    


    Floats
    

    A float is a thread that stays on the same side for several crossings in a row. Long floats make loose cloth that snags. After maxfloat N, every pick checks the new row (weft floats, left to right) and then every column (warp floats, counting all rows so far). The debugger's float strip shows each column's current run.
    


    Errors
    

    The first error stops the program, and the whole output is one line such as error line 5: unknown color 'q'. Studio marks that line in red in the editor. Block problems (bad repeat, unexpected '}', unclosed block) and a missing loom header are found before anything runs; everything else is caught when its line executes.
    


    Keys
    

    Ctrl+Enter runs the program. On the Loom tab, ←/→ step, Space plays or pauses, and Home/End jump to either end.
